what: When the mouse is over a horizontally overflowing strip (overflow-x), a dark DRAG pill (100×36) turns on in .15s in place of the system cursor and sticks to the cursor with no lag. Press and drag and the strip follows the hand sideways (link clicks are ignored past 3px of drag). On release it glides with the last velocity (−0.2 × drag distance) decaying ×.9 per frame. While pressed the pill scales to .92 in .2s. Over links·buttons, or when the strip does not overflow, it turns off in .15s.

options.decay: Multiplier applied to speed each frame, default .9
options.threshold: Drag threshold (px) — beyond it the link press is ignored, default 3
options.[data-fx-part=pill]: (If present) element to use as the pill — if none, the motion part creates one
options.--fx-pill-bg · --fx-pill-ink: Pill background and text color, default --kf-ink-soft 95% · --kf-bg

note: The strip must overflow horizontally for the cursor to turn on (the part opens the overflow with overflow-x: auto). On touch devices no pill is created and horizontal finger swiping (default scroll) is left alone. To turn on the pill over links and buttons too, give that element the class="force-cursor". The original CSS wrote a transition that scales the pill from .5 → 1, but the script overwrites transform with an inline translate, so in practice only opacity changes — I followed that measured, verified behavior.

from.where: index.html .sg-feat__track·.sg-arrival__track — original common.js .drag-scroll(scrollLeft = Start − dx, speed −.2dx, ×.9 on release, |v|<.5 stop) and .custom-cursor (100×36 pill — the inline transform overrides the CSS .5→1, so only opacity .15s, press .92 !important, none at 780px and below)
